notes: The question shares no term with the document that answers it. The lexical adapter cannot reach it and abstains, which is correct behaviour and is the gap the semantic modes are measured against.

qmd's full-text mode reaches no model and abstains on the same question. It is the anchor: the one mode whose empty result is trustworthy, because the reranked modes score an off-corpus query's nearest document at the same value a real hit earns.
Embedding similarity alone finds the document. This is the layer that closes the gap, and isolating it is the point of the mode setting.
Expansion plus RRF fusion over the full-text and vector lists, reranker off. It must rank the same document first; anything it adds over the vector mode on this corpus is what fusion earned.

The whole pipeline, reranker included. If this adds nothing over hybrid on this corpus, the reranker did not earn its place here — which is exactly the evidence a decision about building one into the core needs.
A question in the document's own words. Both adapters must answer it: a semantic source that lost the easy case would have traded away more than it gained.
The same question through qmd's full-text mode. It is the sanity check that this adapter's identity, locators, and relevance agree with the lexical adapter on a case neither can get wrong.

Nothing in the corpus is about this. qmd's full-text mode returns an empty list and Recall abstains, which is the strongest statement any source here can make and the one the reranked modes cannot make honestly.

Nothing in the corpus is about this, and qmd's vector mode does not clear its own cosine threshold for it: the result is an empty list and Recall abstains. That is what makes this mode's cosine usable as Recall's relevance — the admission decision happens in qmd, before any number is reported. hybrid and full cannot make the same statement: their scores are rank-normalized, so rank 1 is 1.0 whatever matched, which is why those two modes keep the lexical recompute.

A lexical source and a semantic source over ONE directory, both returning the same document. They are two views of one file, not two independent pieces of evidence, and the answer must not claim corroboration for it. The two adapters chunk differently by design, so neither the content fingerprint nor the source revision can ever match; what establishes the shared record is the resolved location plus the record identity, which only configuration can see. The document is chosen so both adapters report the SAME title — its H1 is its whole title and it has no subheadings — because the name relation is the only thing that puts two sources' groups in one cluster, and a case without that agreement passes while the defect stands.
